title: Libro de los juegos de ajedrez, dados y tablas
shelf_note: Illuminated 13th-century Castilian manuscript of Alfonso X's chess book; the leaf (miniature of a chess game over two columns of Old Spanish problem text) matches the record. No tradition or collection given to contradict.
structure_note: Record 26 carries folio '8' on the image, which fits rectos-only foliation after front matter. 34 printed numbers in 219 records is what a foliated manuscript gives; the 4 backsteps and 2 repeats are more likely misread or show-through folio numerals than a splice (cannot confirm from one leaf). structure.pages_translated = 0 contradicts pages_translated_field = 189 and this page, which has a translation: one of the counters is wrong (E2).

pages.layout: framed miniature of a chess game across the top; red/blue running head split above it; two columns of Gothic text below with red rubric, large decorated initial L and red/blue paragraph marks; edge of the facing page visible at left

ocr_errors.image: Rey p̃eto / pueto (prieto, 'black'), here and at every 'puesto' on the page
ocr_errors.problem: 'prieto' (black) read throughout as 'puesto' (placed), so the OCR panel never says which side the pieces belong to; the translator corrected it in its meta

ocr_errors.image: the rubric's numeral looks like two x's ('xxvi' or similar); low-resolution red script
ocr_errors.problem: 36 pieces cannot be on a chessboard (32 at most); the numeral is very probably misread, and the English carries it

ocr_errors.problem: 'prietos ... erraren' (if the blacks fail to give check) read as 'primeros ... en uez de' (the first ... instead of); sense roughly recoverable

ocr_errors.image: 'ACE' (red/blue) left and 'DREX' right above the miniature, i.e. 'AÇEDREX'

tr_errors.problem: carries the probable numeral misread; an impossible number of pieces for one board

tr_errors.source: Et si los p̃meros en uez de dar xaque cada uez al Rey blanco
tr_errors.english: And if the first players, instead of giving check to the white king every time, do otherwise
tr_errors.problem: 'the first players' for the blacks, and 'do otherwise' added; the source means 'if the blacks fail to give check each move'. Recoverable, and the summary states it correctly
the head reads 'Açedrex' ('Chess'); the 'Of' comes from the meta's guess 'DE AXEDREX'

other.note: The OCR's <image-desc> is carried into the English as a long <note> describing the miniature, so the reader text opens with an image description
<meta> guesses that the running head is a fragment of 'DE AXEDREX'; both halves of the head ('ACE' + 'DREX') are on this leaf, so it is complete as 'AÇEDREX'

missing.english: placed in the fourth square of the white king
missing.why: the medieval way of naming squares (counted along the file of a named piece, from that side's back rank) is never explained, so none of the move descriptions can be followed on a board

missing.english: they pledge mate to the white king in four of their moves, in his fourth square
missing.why: 'pledge mate ... in his fourth square' is the conventional problem stipulation (mate in N moves on a named square); a reader needs a note on what is being promised

book_verdict: Right leaf, and a good translation that correctly fixes the OCR's systematic 'puesto' for 'prieto' (black). The OCR panel is noticeably wrong, though, and both panes give an impossible 'thirty-six pieces', which is probably a misread numeral.
